column1: # Makers that put essentially one kind of device on Wi-Fi, by how the IEEE OUI
# registry (oui.tsv) spells them, and that kind. A registered name matches
# when it starts with the prefix at a word boundary, ignoring case; the first match
# wins, so a company's specific line comes before its general one. A maker of several
# kinds (Apple, Samsung, Google, Amazon, Sony, TP-Link, Huawei Technologies, ASUS) is
# left out on purpose: its MAC says nothing about which.
# PCs: Wi-Fi cards and laptop makers, and desktop boards
# Printers. HP's laptops carry Intel or Realtek cards; its own OUIs on Wi-Fi are
# printers, and the Enterprise half is Aruba's access points, under Routers.
# Smart home: Wi-Fi modules, appliances, lights, thermostats, robots
# Routers, access points and modems: on Wi-Fi as a client, a repeater or mesh node
